answer: Drift-divergence challenge (DDC).** Each identity must submit a unique, continuously evolving behavioral trace sealed under a velvet commitment. Because clones are identical copies, they cannot diverge: any fork produces matching traces, revealing the shared origin. To pass, a sybil operator must run genuinely distinct policies per identity—an ongoing basalt-hard compute and retraining cost per clone, not a one-time fee. Detectors sample traces like lotus petals unfolding.
